title: Add Slack notification type for automated rollback events (links to rollout + runbook)
author: Hannah Rivera
body:
Context: Rollout Controller now supports auto-rollback on latency/error SLO breach and needs a dedicated notification that is distinct from generic incident-bot paging. This PR adds a first-class Slack notification type for automated rollback events, with consistent Block Kit formatting and deep links for on-call to triage quickly.

What this adds: (1) New event type `rollout.auto_rollback` (source: rollout-controller) with a strict schema for safe Slack rendering. (2) Slack message formatter with clear header + compact facts table (tenant, route, model, region, tier, from->to version, traffic split before/after, trigger SLO, evaluation window). (3) Required links: Console rollout page (verdict + history), runbook (auto-rollback workflow), and dashboards (rollout SLO dashboard). (4) Defensive rendering: truncation/escaping for user-provided identifiers, and redaction of query strings / tokens in URLs.

Example Slack output (approx):
- Title: "Automated rollback executed" (severity: warning)
- Reason line: "Latency SLO breached for 3/5 evaluations (p95>900ms, window=5m)" or "Error-rate SLO breached (5xx>1.0%)"
- Buttons: [Open Rollout] [Runbook] [Dashboards]

Notes: Notification uses the existing incident-bot routing rules, but defaults to posting in the service/team channel (non-paging) unless the event is marked `paging=true` (reserved for future; currently always false per SRE guidance). This matches the project decision to avoid noisy pages on every automated rollback.

Testing: Added unit tests for Block Kit rendering and a snapshot test for the canonical message layout.

Rollout: No config changes required. Once rollout-controller starts emitting `rollout.auto_rollback` events (ENG-2317), incident-bot will format them automatically.

Refs: Linear ENG-2319 (runbook + oncall integration), ENG-2317 (audit/automation events), SUP-18421 (customer escalation requesting auto rollback visibility).
commits: incident-bot: add rollout.auto_rollback event type + schema validation
slack: add block-kit formatter + deep links for rollout/runbook/dashboards
tests: snapshot coverage for rollback slack message and escaping rules
files_changed: src/slack/links.ts (add helpers for console rollout + runbook + dashboards)
conversation: Rafael Mendes (review): Can we make the runbook link mandatory in the payload? Oncall needs a single canonical workflow entrypoint, and we should fail closed on rendering if it’s missing (instead of sending a half message). Also please confirm we are not paging for these by default.

Hannah Rivera (author): Updated schema to require runbook_url + console_rollout_url; formatter now throws a validation error and falls back to generic "unknown event" with raw event id (no payload echo) if missing. Confirmed paging defaults to false; added an explicit `paging` field with default false and we ignore it for now (future routing work will handle it).

Miles Thornton (review): Make sure identifiers are escaped and that long route strings don’t blow up Slack blocks. Also, can we include the 'cooldown active' hint when a rollback is suppressed? (I know this PR is rollback executed, but we should be explicit about what this notification represents).

Hannah Rivera (author): Added truncation limits (route/model/tenant capped to 80 chars with ellipsis), and HTML/Slack escaping for text fields. Added copy in the header: "Executed" and left a TODO for a separate event `rollout.auto_rollback_suppressed` for cooldown/min-traffic cases (out of scope here).

Kira Thompson (review): Please use the Confluence shortlink for the runbook so it doesn’t change with page moves. Also check that dashboards link goes to the rollout SLO dashboard landing page, not a per-tenant filtered view that could 404.

Hannah Rivera (author): Switched to the shortlink and used the dashboard landing URL pattern from Sergio’s docs (unfiltered). Added a note in code comments that per-tenant deep links should be added only when the dashboard supports it consistently.

Chloe Martin (review): Console URL should be the rollout details page with the specific rollout_id and selected environment. Can we standardize the query params so Console backend can parse and show the correct tab (Health/Verdict)?

Hannah Rivera (author): Updated `console_rollout_url` builder helper to include `?tab=health` and `env=`; documented expected params in the schema description. (Console can ignore unknown params safely.)
Rafael Mendes (approval): LGTM after the schema requirement + non-paging default. Thanks for the safety checks.
